The youngest competitor of the day was Ron Hayes (15) who took 3rd place. Ron is 14 months younger than Bicourt and at his present rate of improvement will be quite capable next season of matching(if not beating) John's performances of this year.

He joined in the race after a short distance and finished fourth but did not, of course, score. "Noddy" Edwards and 15 years old Ron Hayes filled the breach admirably, however, and we finished third once again.

Alan Mead won the Junior 880yds in 2:06.8. The Youths finished 5th in their match but found the winner of the mile-----Ron Hayes (4:50.8.).
R.
John Bicourt ran well to gain 4th place in a field of high quality, and he was ably supported by the fast improving Ron Hayes and Bill Bruce.
Ron Hayes set about the opposition like a wild man on Stage two, carrying his bobbing head of unruly hair past no less than 12 opponents to send John Bicourt off in 19th place.
Ron Hayes backed up very well indeed for 9th and with Hurd, Keyes and Bruce packing well in the late 'teens we were assured of second place in the team event.
Ron Hayes made ground with a good run on stage two and John Bicourt, with 3rd fastest time of the day, took us up to 6th and within striking distance of 4th.

In the Youths, Adrian Major, Ron Hayes, Bill Bruce and more recently Derek Hurd have shown considerable potential and if they maintain their progress they could well be strengthening the senior ranks in a few years time.

Ron Hayes ran his best race to date to finish 9th with Adrian Major only one place behind. Despite the forward running of our first three, Walton pipped us for 2nd place by 4 points, thus reducing our final margin to 12 points.
Adrian Major also had a fine run to finish 10th and was ably supported by Ron Hayes (19th) and Derek Hurd (27th) to give us a comfortable 3rd place.
John was well backed up by Adrian Major, 39th,Derek Hurd 54th, and Ron Hayes 75th - the team did wel[illegible] to take 6th place with 186 points.

Hand over fist he closed on the quartet scrambling up to the finish and just managed to split them in two a few yards from the line---another 30yards would have seen him an easy 5th. Adrian Major had a good run to finish 62nd and Ron Hayes produced his usual sound performance to be our 3rd man.

Ron Hayes maintained the good work and galloped into 2nd place some 25 secs. ahead of the Mitcham reserve team, running 6th fastest time. Adrian Major set off, knowing that he was unlikely to make any impression on Badgery of Mitcham, but determined to hold on to 2nd place.

I was very pleased indeed to see two of our boys back again fit and well after a long absence - Ron Hayes and Derek Hurd.Ron has recovered from a serious illness,and tells me that he has now resumed full time work.
